title: Create the two scheduled cycle Routines, disabled

observed_facts: Max instructed 'create the two routines' in a Claude Code session on 2026-08-13

AUTOMATIONS.md and CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT.md define genesis-operator-cycle at 0 13 * * * UTC and genesis-close-cycle at 0 22 * * * UTC, each firing a fresh session with push and email completion notifications
CLOUD_ENVIRONMENT.md section 3 states both Routines remain uncreated or disabled until Day 1 readiness passes
AUTOMATIONS.md previously also required creation itself to wait for both no-write dry runs
Readiness flags operator_schedule_tested and close_schedule_tested are false, and scripts/genesis.py start_cycle blocks every cycle while any readiness flag is false
Protocol status is readiness at protocol version 2.0.0; PREREGISTRATION.md and GENESIS_CHARTER.md are not yet frozen because activation has not occurred
inferences: Creating the Routines in a disabled state satisfies the substantive safety invariant, which is that nothing fires before the dry runs pass
Recording Routine IDs improves auditability because the identifiers are opaque account-scoped references rather than credentials
unknowns: Whether a fired session can push records to main directly, which the dry runs will establish
The Day 1 date, which determines whether the documented November DST shift applies
contrary: Creating before the dry runs departs from the ordering AUTOMATIONS.md originally specified; mitigated by creating them disabled, by amending AUTOMATIONS.md to state the real invariant, and by recording the change here rather than making it silently
A disabled Routine requires a later deliberate enable step, which is a handoff risk; mitigated by naming the enable step as the next permitted action

alternatives: Create the Routines enabled, relying on the start-cycle gate to block early firings
Defer creation until after both dry runs, as AUTOMATIONS.md originally specified
prediction: Both Routines exist, are disabled, fire nothing, and readiness advances to 6 of 13 with the dry runs still outstanding.
decision: Create both Routines against this repository's environment, disable both immediately, record their IDs, and amend AUTOMATIONS.md so that enabling, not creation, is what the dry runs gate.
stop_condition: Stop if either Routine is created enabled and cannot be disabled, if the cron or target environment does not match the documented design, or if validation fails.

title: Fire both Routines once as no-write dry runs

observed_facts: Max instructed 'run both dry runs' in a Claude Code session on 2026-08-13
Both Routines exist and are disabled: genesis-operator-cycle trig_01VqPMDoHhkXgokqw8mLspdb and genesis-close-cycle trig_01BPPQKGmnTp7myYnicRDVap
READINESS.md requires a no-write manual dry run of each branch before either Routine may be enabled
scripts/genesis.py start_cycle evaluates the readiness gate before acquire_lock, so a fired session raises on readiness and never reaches the lock
READINESS_EVIDENCE.md records an unresolved gap: neither Routine stores MCP connectors, so a fired session would lack GitHub issue tools
inferences: Firing each Routine once reproduces a scheduled firing faithfully because the Routine prompt and target environment are identical either way
Because the readiness gate precedes lock acquisition, holding the director lock during the dry runs cannot mask the behavior under test and cannot be damaged by the fired sessions
The dry runs also serve as the diagnostic for the connector gap, since a fired session will demonstrate directly whether GitHub issue tools are present
unknowns: Whether fire_trigger will fire a disabled Routine or require it to be enabled first
Whether a fired session can push to main
Whether a fired session has GitHub issue tools
contrary: A fired session is a live agent in the project environment and could in principle act beyond the intended no-write scope; mitigated by the readiness gate, by the Routine prompts instructing exit on block, by firing sequentially rather than concurrently, and by verifying the remote for unexpected commits afterward

alternatives: Enable both Routines and wait for their natural firings
Simulate the cycles in this session instead of firing fresh sessions
prediction: Each fired session runs start-cycle, is refused by the Day 1 readiness gate, and exits leaving the remote unchanged and the director lock intact.
decision: Fire genesis-operator-cycle once, observe and record, then fire genesis-close-cycle once, observe and record, leaving both Routines disabled throughout.
stop_condition: Stop and record an incident if a fired session changes the remote, acquires or releases the run lock, performs an external write, or begins market research.

scope.expected_outcome: each fired session blocks at the Day 1 readiness gate and exits with no repository changes, no research, and no external action

title: Set both Routines to the preregistered model

observed_facts: The 2026-08-13 dry runs showed both fired sessions served claude-sonnet-5
PREREGISTRATION.md fixes claude-fable-5 at high effort as a preregistered condition, and .claude/settings.json and STATE.json pin the same model
Asked how to correct the model, Max chose 'I set it via update_trigger', which is the explicit owner instruction the model-change control requires
Asked how to correct the connector gap, Max chose to attach the GitHub connector in the claude.ai Routines UI, which is owner-side work the director cannot perform
inferences: Setting the Routine model to the preregistered value restores the fixed-configuration condition rather than altering it
A dry run repeated now would still fail on the connector gap, so re-testing should wait until Max reports the connector attached
unknowns: Whether the provider surfaces the configured model on the Routine record before its next firing
When the GitHub connector will be attached
contrary: Changing a Routine's model is normally outside the director's initiative; mitigated because the owner chose this option explicitly and the target value is the preregistered one

alternatives: Have Max recreate both Routines in the UI with the model set
Leave the model unset and accept whatever the scheduler serves
prediction: Both Routines will be configured for claude-fable-5, and the repeated dry runs will confirm it once the connector is attached.
decision: Set model claude-fable-5 on both Routines, leave them disabled, and defer the repeat dry runs until Max reports the GitHub connector attached.
stop_condition: Stop if either update is rejected, if the update alters schedule, prompt, or enabled state, or if validation fails.
